meta.title: Light-sheet tracking of every cell in the zebrafish embryo
meta.reviewed: Written by hand from source/manuscript.md: the figure style (black, true fluorescence colours added together, white scale bars and monospaced time stamps, Manrope) is the look; the legend's four panels are the scenes.

source.notes: fictional imaging article: abstract, Figure 1 legend (a-d), key numbers, figure style
simulated nuclei of a 10-hpf embryo and 300 lineage tracks 6-24 hpf (paper-src/simulate.py)

rationale.palette: Microscopy on black: nuclei magenta (#FF3EC8), membranes cyan (#2EE6FF), the notochord reporter green (#4BFF6A), added together so overlaps glow white; UI in white at reduced opacity, never coloured.
rationale.type: Manrope for sentences, DM Mono for every scale bar, time stamp and channel name, as the figure style says.
rationale.motion: Patient and smooth: a slow turntable, a light sheet that scans at an even pace, tracks that grow with a running hpf clock; easing ioSine, no hits except the moment the three channels register.
rationale.sound: Wonder, not tension: ambient at 92 BPM in E lydian, pad, glass and bell, soft kick.
rationale.visuals: The embryo as 2,400 glowing nuclei: they gather and the channels register; the light sheet slices it with a live 2D section; 300 lineage tracks from 6 to 24 hpf; the commitment timeline makes the claim.
